sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details a coordinated card-not-present fraud scheme targeting customer C06220 on card C06220-K1, alongside related unauthorized transactions identified across peer cards C05061-K1, C07925-K1, and C10553-K1. Between January 17, 2017, and January 19, 2017, card C06220-K1 incurred three unauthorized online purchases for product C totaling $2,166.71. The sequential charges comprised transaction 3660125 for $637.13 on January 17 in region 330, transaction 3660126 for $758.80 on January 18 in region 384, and transaction 3660127 for $770.78 on January 19 in region 126. Each unauthorized transaction was conducted through a new device identifier—D009715, D009718, and D009721 respectively—and routed through anonymous internet proxy connections (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS). The perpetrator also varied the associated contact emails across domains including anonymous.com, comcast.net, and verizon.net. This activity marked a complete departure from the cardholder's historical baseline, which contained zero product-C transactions across the prior 60 days. Scheme analysis revealed that three cards belonging to distinct customers—C05061-K1, C07925-K1, and C10553-K1—experienced the identical pattern of repeated online product-C charges between $510 and $963 from new devices behind anonymous proxies between January 12, 2017, and January 17, 2017. The deliberate rotation of device identifiers and IP proxies across multiple customer accounts demonstrates an organized syndicated effort to evade automated fraud filters and single-device link detection. Card C06220-K1 has been blocked, connected accounts have been placed under monitoring, and this filing is submitted under Policy R9 for undocumented coordinated fraud.

passages.section: Section 3a. A case is not a report
passages.text: Section 3a. A case is not a report. Two different things, and the agent produces both. **A case** (`CREATE_CASE`) is the bank's internal record of an investigation. Open one whenever fraud probability reaches 0.30, whenever you request evidence, or whenever a customer disputes a charge. A case can be closed as fraud or as legitimate. It can be updated when new evidence arrives. It should be written into the graph so later investigations can find it: a case that names a merchant or a device becomes evidence for the next analyst. **A suspicious activity report** (`FILE_REPORT`) is a regulatory filing sent outside the bank. File one when fraud is confirmed or strongly suspected **and** at least one of these holds: exposure exceeds $1,000; the activity connects to a shared device profile, a shared region cluster, or another customer's fraud; the pattern is coordinated or undocumented (rule R9). A report always has a case behind it. Most cases never need a report. The report narrative must stand on its own: who, what, when, where, how, and why it is suspicious. Deciding correctly between ""case only"" and ""case plus report"" is part of the next-best-action score.

Rule R9: Undocumented patterns. When activity fits none of the known patterns but the evidence shows coordinated or repeated abuse across customers, recommend `CREATE_CASE`, `FILE_REPORT`, and `ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST`, and describe the pattern in your own words. Do not force it into a known category.

Rule R6: Shared origin. When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.
